facts.F1: Bug #6624: in a browser whose time zone is west of UTC (for example anywhere in the Americas), the Delivery dialog refuses tomorrow as a launch date and says the date must be in the future. Only the day after tomorrow is accepted. Repro: set the browser or OS time zone to e.g. America/New_York, open a Portfolio, create a Delivery, pick tomorrow's date: Save stays blocked with the future-date message. Expected: tomorrow is accepted in every time zone; today stays refused.
facts.F10: Choosing a past date as a launch date is refused in every time zone.
facts.F15: With the browser clock in New York, early in the morning and late in the evening when the UTC date is already the next day, the launch-date rule and the Save gate (a named launch with a feature picked) are asked about today, tomorrow, yesterday and a month ago, written as the day strings the date field holds; two days that are not on any calendar (month 13 and month 00) are asked about too
facts.F16: Tomorrow is accepted with no date error and Save is open; today, yesterday and a month ago are refused, and Save is blocked for today, with the message that the launch date must be in the future; a day with no such month is refused, never rolled into another year
facts.F17: A user in the Americas can save a Delivery dated tomorrow; today and past dates stay blocked; a mistyped month cannot be saved
facts.F18: A fix that accepts every future-looking date including today, only works at one time of day, fixes the field rule but not the Save gate, or accepts a month that rolls over is caught by the today and far-past rows, the two clock moments, the Save gate row and the impossible-month rows; an east-of-UTC run is caught by the offset check
facts.F19: Probe frontend-tests deliveryFormRules: passing rows for the launch-date rule: no date, yesterday, today and tomorrow each judged by whether after today; yesterday, today and tomorrow each answered with the message that names its fix. No failing row in the output shown; output cut at 6000 bytes by my head filter.
facts.F2: A team lead in any time zone can save a Delivery that launches tomorrow, and still cannot save one for today or the past.
facts.F20: Probe frontend-tests westOfUtc: 1 file, 7 of 7 passed. Passing rows: clock-behind-UTC guard; tomorrow accepted and today and past refused in early morning and in late evening when UTC is already the next day; named launch dated tomorrow saved and today blocked; 2027-13-01 and 2027-00-10 refused as not on any calendar.
facts.F21: Limit: no Delivery dialog in a browser was driven. Only Vitest rule-level rows under a faked west-of-UTC clock were observed. I did not capture the YYYY-MM-DD stimulus or its response myself, no time zone other than the faked clock, and no verbatim error text. Row names and pass marks are project test-suite output, not user-observed behavior.
facts.F22: Non-probe: E1, E2 and E3 at dialog level (typed YYYY-MM-DD in the Delivery dialog, clock in America/New_York, tomorrow/today/yesterday) were not probed; no browser probe exists on the public surface. Only rule-level rows were observed.
facts.F3: Tomorrow is accepted as a launch date in every time zone; today and the past stay refused
facts.F4: In a browser west of UTC, the Delivery dialog accepts tomorrow as a launch date and still refuses today and the past
facts.F5: With the clock in America/New_York, the launch-date rule is asked about today, tomorrow and yesterday, each written as the YYYY-MM-DD string the date field holds
facts.F6: Tomorrow is accepted with no date error; today and yesterday are refused with '<Delivery term> date must be in the future'
facts.F7: Tomorrow is refused as not in the future, or today is accepted, while the clock is west of UTC
facts.F8: A user in any time zone, including zones west of UTC, can choose tomorrow's date as a launch date and it is accepted.
facts.F9: Choosing today's date as a launch date is refused in every time zone.
